title: SYSK Live from SXSW: How UFOs Work
summary: Live SXSW taping in Austin, Texas, in which Josh and Chuck discuss how UFOs work and the history of UFO phenomena. Topics include ancient and medieval airship accounts, the 1880s-1890s airship sightings, the 2011 Jerusalem sighting, the Air Force's Project Sign, Grudge and Blue Book investigations, the Air Force's 1969 closure statement, astronomer J. Allen Hynek and his UFO definition and Close Encounters scale, Charles Fort, the Roswell incident of July 1947, Area 51, Men in Black, celebrity UFO sightings (Reagan, Jackie Gleason, Carter), the Betty and Barney Hill abduction case, and skeptical explanations such as sleep paralysis, false awakenings, and temporal lobe stimulation. The episode includes a live audience poll on belief in aliens.
topics: close encounters of the third kind

segments.title: Opening banter and X-Files tie-in
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the live SXSW taping in Austin, Texas, joking about the audience and the X-Files. They describe ancient Indian Sanskrit texts and a 1211 English church airship story as early UFO-like accounts, and mention the 2011 Jerusalem sighting and the Mutual UFO Network.

segments.title: Air Force UFO investigations and the term UFO
segments.summary: The term UFO was coined by the US Air Force. The Air Force investigated about 12,000 sightings from 1940s to 1960s, with 701 left unexplained. Common explanations include weather balloons, lightning, and hoaxes.

segments.title: J. Allen Hynek and the UFO definition
segments.summary: Astronomer J. Allen Hynek, initially a skeptic hired by the Air Force, became an outspoken proponent after reviewing the files. The hosts read his definition of a UFO. They describe Project Sign, Project Grudge, and Project Blue Book, and Charles Fort's influence on Hynek's views.

segments.title: Hynek scale and close encounters
segments.summary: Hynek's scale, known as the close encounters chart, ranks sightings by kind: first kind (sighting), second kind (physical evidence), third kind (animate beings), and later additions including abduction, human contact, injury or death, and sexual contact. Physical traces such as disintegrated vegetation and spider-web-like strings are mentioned.
topics: close encounters of the third kind

segments.title: Cattle mutilations, interference, and sighting statistics
segments.summary: The hosts discuss cattle mutilations and a 1970s Arkansas case in which a dead cow was filmed and explained by natural decomposition. They also mention radio and TV interference and car failures, then cover UFO sighting counts by state, with New Mexico and California leading and North Dakota lowest.

segments.title: Live audience poll on belief in aliens
segments.summary: Chuck runs a live applause poll of the audience on whether aliens have contacted humans, abducted humans, or whether the government is hiding something. The hosts cite a 2008 poll and compare belief to Y2K anxiety.

segments.title: Air Force closes Project Blue Book
segments.summary: In 1969 the Air Force closed Project Blue Book with a statement that no UFO showed a threat to national security and no evidence showed sightings were extraterrestrial. The hosts discuss the wording and note that SETI and the Center for UFO Studies continued the research.

segments.title: Roswell incident
segments.summary: On July 7, 1947, rancher Mac Brazel found debris near Roswell, New Mexico, after thunderstorms and strange lights. The sheriff called the military, and the Roswell Army Air Force Base first announced a crashed disc, then a later statement called it a weather balloon. Eyewitness accounts of bodies and an alien autopsy film are mentioned, along with Area 51.

segments.title: Men in Black and X-Files episode
segments.summary: The hosts describe Men in Black as a phenomenon that originated in Gray Barker's 1956 book They Knew Too Much About Flying Saucers, which was fiction. They recommend an X-Files episode featuring Men in Black characters.

segments.title: Celebrity UFO sightings
segments.summary: The hosts discuss UFO sightings claimed by Ronald Reagan, Jimmy Carter, and Jackie Gleason. Gleason reportedly said Richard Nixon took him to see aliens, which he later told his wife about.

segments.title: Alien abduction history and skeptical explanations
segments.summary: The hosts cover the Betty and Barney Hill case from the early 1960s, the first widely reported abduction, which was recovered through hypnosis and later adapted into a TV movie. Richard McNally found abductees showed PTSD-like symptoms. Susan Blackmore's temporal lobe experiment with Michael Persinger is covered, along with sleep paralysis and false awakenings as explanations.

segments.title: Wrap-up and sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck wrap up, say the topic is wholly unexplained, and plan follow-ups on Area 51 and abductions. They invite email to the show and close with the show's website and app promotion.
